dek.text: Houston Methodist put four AI cameras in each room of a {{number:c2}} room heart surgery suite. A study ties them to more cases a month and names its own limits.

introduction.text: [The study covers a {{number:c2}} room cardiothoracic operating suite at Houston Methodist Hospital](c2). [Each operating room there was fitted with four high resolution wall mounted cameras](c3). [The hospital says the cameras identify and timestamp workflow steps](c22). [The system texts surgeons when a patient arrives, when the patient is draped and when the case ends](c23).

[The study was published in the Journal of Imaging on {{date:c1}}](c1). [It estimates the deployment was associated with about {{number:c6}} more cases a month](c6). [That is roughly {{number:c7}} over a baseline of about {{number:c7:1}} cases a month](c7).

paragraphs.text: [The software went live at Walter Tower in December {{number:c4}}](c4). [The study window ran {{number:c5}} months with {{number:c5:1}} before deployment and {{number:c5:2}} after](c5). [It covered {{number:c5:3}} surgical cases at the suite](c5).
[The estimate's {{number:c6:1}} confidence interval runs from {{number:c6:2}} to {{number:c6:3}} more cases a month](c6).

[The detection system was trained on {{number:c20}} surgical cases from {{number:c20:1}} operating rooms](c20). [During a learning period a human led quality control team confirmed the locations and actions it identified](c21).

[The authors call the rise associated with the deployment rather than caused by it](c10). [A change management program came with the cameras, and the study can't attribute the gains to either one alone](c11).

[In a placebo test Walter Tower ranked second of {{number:c8}} units](c8). [The authors write that this result points the same way as the main estimate and does not reach conventional statistical significance](c9). [A sensitivity analysis found no significant change in total operative minutes a month](c12). [The hospital's blog says turnover times fell while operative minutes did not](c24).

[The paper names Apella Technology as the vendor of the system it evaluates](c28). [Houston Methodist holds a minority equity interest in Apella](c13). [An Apella employee ran the original analyses](c14). [A Houston Methodist analyst then replicated them on the same aggregated dataset](c15). [The paper says Apella did not fund the study and had no role beyond those analyses](c16).

[The paper says video is kept for at most {{number:c17}} days and audio for at most {{number:c17:1}}](c17). [Recordings from incision to skin closure are open to three designated roles](c18). [The surgeon is told whenever one of them is reviewed](c19).

[The hospital's blog says staff raised concerns about surveillance, data security and privacy](c25). [It says signs are posted in operating rooms and patient consent is folded into universal consent for care](c26). Neither the paper nor the blog says whether a patient can ask not to be recorded.
